decisions.decision: Column-vs-jsonb rule: a value gets its own column iff Postgres must filter, join, order, or enforce uniqueness/FK on it, OR a concurrent writer can edit it independently of its siblings. Everything else that one owner reads and writes as a whole object is jsonb, validated by a zod discriminated union at the HTTP boundary before it reaches the DB.
decisions.rationale: The second clause is the lost-update clause: mcphub's whole-blob rewrite (dao/base/JsonFileBaseDao.ts:17-77) loses concurrent edits. Anything two humans can touch at once gets a row.
decisions.cost: Transport config lives in jsonb, so you cannot SQL-query `WHERE command = 'npx'`. Acceptable: nothing needs to.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's own AGENTS.md says one persisted field touches SEVEN layers. Here it touches one zod schema and nothing else, or one column plus one generated migration.

decisions.decision: `secrets` is the ONLY encrypted store in the system. `credential_bindings` and `upstream_oauth_tokens` hold metadata and point at a `secrets.id`; server env/headers hold `{"$secret":"<uuid>"}` inside `servers.config`. Plaintext secret values are never representable in any other column.
decisions.rationale: mcphub has three encryption stories — AES-GCM for credential bindings (credentialBindingService.ts:18-118) and plaintext for everything else (oauthSettingsStore.ts:107-129, BearerKey.ts:21). One table means one crypto path, one AAD scheme, one rotation job.
decisions.cost: Every secret read is a join or a second query. Core caches resolved config per (server, revision), so it is one query per connect, not per call.

decisions.decision: `upstream_oauth_tokens` stays a separate table; the upstream client REGISTRATION (CIMD url / DCR client_id + client secret ref) collapses into `servers.config.oauth`.
decisions.rationale: Grants are queried by (server_id, user_id) and swept by `expires_at < now()`, and they carry filterable non-secret metadata (issuer, resource, scopes) — that is exactly D1's column test. Registration is one blob per server that is never filtered, so it is jsonb and one table disappears.

decisions.decision: Per-tool/prompt/resource enable + description override is a normalized table `server_item_override` keyed (server_id, kind, item_name) on the BARE upstream name, never a jsonb map on `servers`.
decisions.rationale: Call-time enforcement (their CVE fix afcc72f) becomes an indexed PK lookup instead of blob parsing, and one operator toggling a tool cannot clobber another's edit. Storing only bare names is why we do not need mcphub's check-under-both-bare-and-prefixed-keys hack (mcpService.ts:3388).

decisions.decision: The namespace separator is the fixed constant `__`, not config, and `servers.slug` / `groups.slug` / `group_server.alias` carry a DB CHECK `~ '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$'` that excludes `_`. Split the exposed name at the FIRST `__`.
decisions.rationale: mcphub only WARNS about server names (mcpService.ts:1710) with a configurable separator (config/index.ts:256), so two names differing by separator chars can alias into each other's tools. A CHECK constraint makes that unrepresentable and no code path can bypass it.
decisions.cost: Server slugs cannot contain underscores. Display `name` is free-form, so nobody notices.

decisions.decision: No `sharedWithUsers[]`. `visibility` is a NOT NULL enum `private|team|public`, `owner_id` is NOT NULL. Groups are the only narrower-than-team sharing mechanism in v1.
decisions.rationale: mcphub's two divergent authz paths (dataService.ts:6-28 vs DaoConfigService:171, where `owner === undefined` is visible to everyone) and `group.visibility == null` opening a route (utils/groupAccess.ts:6) are both open-by-omission bugs; NOT NULL deletes the entire class. A team self-host does not need per-user ACLs on day one.

decisions.decision: `tool_embedding` is the single cached catalog for tools AND prompts AND resources, carrying `input_schema`, `token_cost`, the tsvector and the nullable vector in one row. There is no separate tool cache, no separate embedding table, and no live-recompute cost service.
decisions.rationale: mcphub keeps the tool cache in memory, embeddings in VectorEmbedding, and Context Cost as a live non-persisted aggregation (contextCostService.ts:76-95) — three copies of the same fact. One table makes context cost a `SELECT sum(token_cost)` and makes search a single scoped query.
decisions.cost: Prompts/resources carry a NULL embedding forever. They still rank lexically, which is all the UI search box needs.

decisions.rationale: At hundreds to low-thousands of tools IVFFlat is actively wrong: it needs training data that does not exist at install time and recall collapses when `lists` is tiny, so it must be rebuilt after every sync. HNSW is correct from row zero, builds incrementally, and costs about 13 MB at 2k x 1536.
decisions.cost: Slower bulk build. At 2k rows that is milliseconds.

decisions.decision: `audit_event` is unpartitioned, has NO foreign keys, and denormalizes server/group/key/user display names. Retention is two-tier: payloads scrubbed at PAYLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7), rows deleted at AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 90), both by an hourly batched statement.
decisions.rationale: An append-only log must outlive every row it references — an FK with SET NULL would silently destroy attribution when a key is revoked, which is the exact moment you need the log. Two-tier retention keeps 90 days of latency metrics while payloads (the only PII-bearing columns) live a week.
decisions.cost: ponytail: unpartitioned DELETE-based retention bloats past roughly 50M rows; upgrade is a custom migration to monthly RANGE partitions with PK (started_at, id) and DROP TABLE reclaim.

interfaces.name: packages/core/src/db/schema/_shared.ts
interfaces.notes: pgEnum ceiling: adding a value is `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` (drizzle-kit generates it), and PG will not let you USE the new value in the same transaction that added it — so an enum-widening migration must be its own file with nothing after it.

interfaces.name: packages/core/src/db/schema/auth.ts
interfaces.notes: Hard rule: never hand-edit auth-schema.ts. On a better-auth upgrade, re-run generate; the CI `git diff --exit-code` gate turns any schema drift into a reviewed migration instead of a silent `synchronize:true` alter (mcphub db/connection.ts:92).

interfaces.name: servers
interfaces.notes: No status/lastError/toolCount columns. Live connection state stays in core memory (mcphub's module-level serverInfos, mcpService.ts:733, is the right shape) — a status column in Postgres is a cross-replica lie. allowPrivateNetwork is the ONLY SSRF bypass and it is per-server, NOT per-owner: mcphub bypasses assertSafeUrl for any admin-owned server (mcpService.ts:1382-1396), which makes every admin-created server an unguarded fetcher by accident.

interfaces.name: packages/core/src/db/schema/config-schema.ts (the servers.config jsonb contract)
interfaces.notes: `.strict()` everywhere: an unknown key is a 400, not a silently persisted blob. This zod parse is the trust boundary for the jsonb column — the DB CHECK only verifies `type` agrees, zod verifies the rest. No `${VAR}` / `$VAR` process.env expansion (mcphub config/index.ts:150-252): env interpolation is how plaintext secrets end up in a config file. Use a SecretRef.

interfaces.name: server_item_override
interfaces.notes: The PK is the only index needed; it serves both the per-server load at cache time and the single-row CALL-time gate. CALL time is the point: the gate runs inside the resolver that finds the tool, not only inside the list projection (mcphub afcc72f / mcpService.ts:3388) — and a disabled item raises the SAME `ToolUnavailableError` text as a nonexistent one (mcphub :2654), while `audit_event.error_code` records the true reason ('item_disabled' vs 'item_unknown'). Identical outward, distinguishable inward.

interfaces.name: groups + group_server
interfaces.notes: ponytail: the alias-collides-with-another-member's-real-slug case is checked in the write path, not by a constraint (a unique index cannot span the alias column and the other table's slug). Ceiling: a stale read could let two concurrent writes collide; upgrade is a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger or a generated `exposed_slug` column materialised as `coalesce(alias, <slug>)` with a unique index on (group_id, exposed_slug). Route resolution order is groups.slug -> servers.slug -> empty=all, with `$smart` reserved — so `groups.slug` and `servers.slug` share a namespace and 'smart' / '$smart' must be rejected by the slug write path.

interfaces.name: secrets
interfaces.notes: Cascade from `servers` and `user` is how orphaned secrets are collected — a DB constraint instead of a cleanup job (mcphub has neither: oauthSettingsStore.ts:107-168 leaves plaintext tokens in the config blob forever). No `last_used_at`: that is what audit_event is for. Rotation: `key_version` is already on the row; a rotation pass is a `SELECT ... WHERE key_version < $current` re-encrypt loop over a few hundred rows, no index needed.

interfaces.name: credential_bindings
interfaces.notes: ON DELETE RESTRICT on secretId (not cascade) so a secret can never be deleted out from under a live binding; deleting the binding row deletes the secret in the same transaction, explicitly. Slot names bound here MUST be stripped from any passthrough header set before the upstream call (mcphub credentialBindingService.ts:225-238) — otherwise a caller can override someone else's credential by sending the same header. A server with credentialMode='per_user' and no binding for the caller DENIES the call; it does not silently fall back to the shared secret (mcphub's `credentialEligible:false` is fail-open by omission for any new auth path).

interfaces.name: upstream_oauth_tokens
interfaces.notes: Two partial unique indexes instead of a sentinel uuid — NULL means "the server's shared grant" and stays NULL. The in-flight PKCE code_verifier is NOT here and is not persisted at all: it lives in the auth flow's short-lived state for the seconds between /authorize and /token. mcphub persists it plaintext into the server config blob (oauthSettingsStore.ts:107-168), which is a stored replay primitive for zero benefit.

interfaces.name: audit_event
interfaces.notes: Payloads are VERBATIM when enabled, never heuristically redacted (mcphub activityLoggingService.ts:112-118 is right: a regex scrubber gives false confidence). Controls instead: off by default via system_setting `audit.storePayloads`; ALWAYS null when credentialMode='per_user' or 'passthrough' (mcphub :70-75); 100 KB cap enforced in the writer with payloadOmittedReason='too_large' (mcphub :142). `inputKeys` is recorded unconditionally — you can answer "did anyone pass a `path` argument" without storing one byte of content. No `sourceIp` as text: `inet` is correct for IPv6 and for CIDR queries.

interfaces.name: audit retention (packages/core/src/db/retention.ts)
interfaces.sketch:
-- Runs hourly from one node (whoever holds pg_try_advisory_lock(4823002)).
-- Two tiers: payloads die young, metrics live long.

-- 1. scrub payloads (default 7 days). Cheap UPDATE, keeps the row + metrics.
UPDATE audit_event
   SET input_payload = NULL, output_payload = NULL,
       payload_omitted_reason = 'expired'
 WHERE started_at < now() - ($1 || ' days')::interval
   AND (input_payload IS NOT NULL OR output_payload IS NOT NULL);

-- 2. delete rows (default 90 days), batched so we never hold a long lock.
WITH doomed AS (
  SELECT id FROM audit_event
   WHERE started_at < now() - ($2 || ' days')::interval
   ORDER BY started_at
   LIMIT 10000
)
DELETE FROM audit_event a USING doomed d WHERE a.id = d.id;
-- repeat until 0 rows affected, max 50 iterations per tick.
interfaces.notes: Both windows come from system_setting (`audit.payloadRetentionDays`, `audit.retentionDays`), not env, because an operator changes them at runtime. ponytail: DELETE-based retention, ceiling ~50M rows / autovacuum keeping up. Upgrade path is a custom migration converting audit_event to monthly RANGE partitions on started_at (PK becomes (started_at, id), drizzle-kit cannot generate PARTITION BY so it is a hand-written file) and swapping step 2 for DROP TABLE. mcphub's equivalent is a manual `DELETE /api/activities/cleanup?daysOld=` an operator has to remember to call.

interfaces.name: tool_embedding
interfaces.notes: The (server_id, kind, item_name) unique index also serves every per-server load and the join from group_server, so there is no separate server_id index. No server-level embedding row: the server slug/name/description is already prefixed into every item's search_text, which captures most of mcphub's 0.8*tool + 0.2*server blend (vectorSearchService.ts:1496) for zero extra rows and zero extra query.

interfaces.name: HNSW vs IVFFlat, and how a NULL embedding still ranks
interfaces.sketch:
-- INDEX CHOICE, for a real team install of 300-3000 items:
--   ivfflat needs `lists ~= rows/1000` and must be BUILT ON POPULATED DATA.
--   At 2k rows that is lists=2: recall collapses, and every catalog resync
--   invalidates the centroids, so you owe a REINDEX after every sync.
--   hnsw is correct from row zero, builds incrementally on INSERT, and costs
--   ~13 MB at 2000 x 1536 float4. Build time at that size: milliseconds.
-- Query-time knob: SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = 40;
-- Small selective scopes: SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = 'relaxed_order';
--   (or just let the planner seq-scan a 200-row scope — at this size it wins)

-- HYBRID SEARCH. Scope is pushed into BOTH branches BEFORE LIMIT.
-- $1 query text, $2 query vector, $3 scope: (server_id, item_name|null) pairs
WITH scope(server_id, item_name) AS (SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($3::jsonb)
                                       AS x(server_id uuid, item_name text)),
visible AS (
  SELECT te.*
    FROM tool_embedding te
    JOIN scope s ON s.server_id = te.server_id
                AND (s.item_name IS NULL OR s.item_name = te.item_name)
    LEFT JOIN server_item_override o
           ON o.server_id = te.server_id AND o.kind = te.kind
          AND o.item_name = te.item_name
    JOIN servers sv ON sv.id = te.server_id AND sv.enabled
   WHERE te.kind = 'tool' AND coalesce(o.enabled, true)
),
lex AS (
  SELECT id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(tsv, q) DESC) AS r
    FROM visible, websearch_to_tsquery('english', $1) q
   WHERE tsv @@ q
   LIMIT 50
),
vec AS (
  SELECT id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY embedding <=> $2::vector) AS r
    FROM visible
   WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL
   ORDER BY embedding <=> $2::vector
   LIMIT 50
)
SELECT id, coalesce(1.0/(60 + lex.r), 0) + coalesce(1.0/(60 + vec.r), 0) AS score
  FROM lex FULL OUTER JOIN vec USING (id)
 ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT $4;
interfaces.notes: A NULL-embedding row appears only in `lex` and scores 1/(60+r) from reciprocal-rank fusion alone — it ranks, it just never gets the vector boost. That is what makes the vector column optional: with no embedding provider configured at all, search still works lexically instead of falling back to mcphub's 100-dim hash embeddings (vectorSearchService.ts:1029), which are noise dressed as semantics. RRF k=60 is the standard constant; the routing agent owns tuning it.

interfaces.name: EMBEDDING_DIM change + CREATE EXTENSION ordering
interfaces.notes: Boot refuses to start on a dim mismatch rather than inserting and letting pgvector throw per-row at sync time — a loud failure at t=0 beats a search feature that is quietly half-empty.

interfaces.name: catalog_cache + system_setting
interfaces.notes: system_setting.value is jsonb with a per-key zod schema in a single `SETTINGS` record; the write endpoint looks the key up and parses, so an unknown key is a 400 and a bad value never reaches the DB. Discovery disabled returns 404, not 401 — deliberately unprobeable (mcphub discoveryController.ts:23-31 gets this right).

interfaces.name: drizzle.config.ts + package scripts + CI gate
interfaces.notes: Migration files are committed artifacts, never regenerated in place — drizzle-kit only ever appends. Anyone who needs to change an applied migration writes a new one. No `synchronize:true` equivalent exists anywhere in this codebase (mcphub db/connection.ts:92 has it on, plus hand-written DDL for vector_embeddings at :217-263 because synchronize cannot express it — that split is exactly what real migration files delete).

interfaces.name: packages/core/src/db/migrate.ts
interfaces.notes: A dedicated pg.Client, not the pool: pg_advisory_lock is session-scoped and a pooled checkout gives you a different session on the next query. drizzle's node-postgres migrator does not take any lock of its own, which is why boot on three replicas at once needs this. The verify-when-not-applying half is the part people skip and then spend an afternoon debugging a column that does not exist.

interfaces.name: first-admin bootstrap (packages/core/src/db/bootstrap.ts)
interfaces.notes: Restarting before the token is claimed mints a fresh one (onConflictDoUpdate), so an abandoned token cannot linger. Everything else — roles beyond admin/member, what admin can do — is the auth agent's.

interfaces.name: packages/core/src/db/migrate.test.ts (the one runnable check)
interfaces.notes: Runs in CI against a real pgvector image, which is exactly the job mcphub has DISABLED (.github/workflows/ci.yml:48-113) — so their DB mode, pgvector routing and activity logging are only ever exercised against sqlite::memory:. This one test is the difference.

summary: Eleven of our tables plus better-auth's generated ten, in one Drizzle migration chain with real committed SQL files. The single idea that makes it leaner than mcphub: every fact lives in exactly one place, and the places Postgres can enforce a rule, it does. One `secrets` table is the only encrypted store (mcphub has one AES path and three plaintext ones); one `tool_embedding` row carries the tool cache, its token cost and both search indexes (mcphub has three separate copies, one of them not persisted at all); NOT NULL on `owner_id`/`visibility` and a slug CHECK excluding the `__` separator make mcphub's open-by-omission and name-aliasing bug classes unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely. mcphub's own AGENTS.md says adding one persisted field touches seven layers; here it touches one zod schema, or one column and one generated migration. No JSON mode, no dual DAO, no `synchronize:true`.

deferred.add_when: a scoped search demonstrably misses whole servers whose tools are named unlike the query — the server slug/name/description is already prefixed into every item's search_text
a team asks for sharing narrower than a group but wider than private; visibility private|team|public plus groups covers v1

deferred.item: audit_event monthly RANGE partitions (PK becomes (started_at, id), hand-written migration)
deferred.add_when: the table passes ~50M rows or the hourly batched DELETE stops keeping up
the 24h latency/error tile computed from audit_server_idx exceeds ~500ms

deferred.item: Secret key rotation job (key_version is already on every row)
deferred.add_when: the first rotation — it is a SELECT WHERE key_version < current, decrypt, re-encrypt loop over a few hundred rows
tsvector lexical search is observed missing real typo'd queries; adds an extension that needs the same DDL rights as vector

risks: `CREATE EXTENSION vector` needs superuser/rds_superuser; a locked-down managed Postgres hits this on migration 0000. IF NOT EXISTS plus MIGRATE_ON_BOOT=false covers it, but it is the first thing an enterprise operator trips over.

better-auth's generated auth-schema.ts will shift between minors and produce a migration on every upgrade. The `git diff --exit-code` gate catches drift, but the review burden on a table we do not own is real.

pgEnum widening needs `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` in its own migration file — PG will not let the new value be used in the transaction that added it, so a widening migration must have nothing after it.
The `servers_type_matches_config` CHECK couples a column to jsonb contents; a hand-written UPDATE to config that omits `type` fails confusingly. Always write both, or write neither via the API.

Changing embedding model to one with a different dimension requires a hand-written ALTER migration and an index rebuild. Boot refuses to start rather than mis-ranking — loud, but it is a downtime event unless the operator uses Matryoshka truncation.
security: Plaintext secret values are unrepresentable outside `secrets`: server env/headers hold only `{"$secret":"<uuid>"}`, enforced by the `.strict()` zod union on the jsonb column. No `${VAR}`/`$VAR` process.env expansion (mcphub config/index.ts:150-252) — that mechanism is how secrets end up in a config file.

AAD is the columns themselves (scope|serverId|userId|label|keyVersion, \x1f-joined). A ciphertext row copied to another server, another user or another slot fails to decrypt. CHECK constraints pin iv to 12 bytes and tag to 16, so a truncated-tag forgery cannot even be stored.

`owner_id` NOT NULL and `visibility` NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' make mcphub's two open-by-omission bugs impossible to represent: `owner === undefined` visible to everyone (DaoConfigService:171) and `group.visibility == null` opening a route to any authenticated caller (utils/groupAccess.ts:6).

Slug CHECK `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$` excludes `_`, and the separator is the fixed constant `__`. Two servers cannot alias into each other's namespaced tool names — mcphub only WARNS (mcpService.ts:1710) with a configurable separator (config/index.ts:256).

`allowPrivateNetwork` is per-server and defaults false. It is the ONLY SSRF bypass and it is never derived from who owns the server — mcphub bypasses assertSafeUrl for any admin-owned server (mcpService.ts:1382-1396), which silently disarms the guard for the most privileged creator.

`secrets` and `credential_bindings` have no read path from the HTTP API: only core's config resolver SELECTs them. Credential slots are write-only from the UI, and a bound slot name is stripped from any caller-supplied passthrough header before the upstream call (mcphub credentialBindingService.ts:225-238) so a caller cannot override someone else's credential.

`credentialMode='per_user'` with no binding for the caller DENIES; it never falls back to the shared secret. mcphub's `credentialEligible:false` is fail-open by omission for any newly added auth path.

audit_event has no foreign keys and denormalizes user/key/server names, so revoking a key or deleting a server cannot erase or blank the trail. Payload columns are nullable by design, off by default, always NULL for credentialed calls, capped at 100 KB, and `payload_omitted_reason` records why — but `input_keys` is recorded unconditionally so "did anyone pass a `path` argument" is answerable without storing content.

A disabled item and a nonexistent item produce identical client-facing error text; the true reason goes to `audit_event.error_reason` ('item_disabled' vs 'item_unknown'). Identical outward, distinguishable inward.
No seeded credentials. First admin is a 256-bit one-time token printed to the boot log, claimed via a `DELETE ... RETURNING` on system_setting that is itself the mutex — mcphub ships admin/admin123.
phase: Phase 1 — data layer. Blocks every other subsystem: core cannot load a server, routing cannot search, observability cannot write, and auth cannot store a key until this chain applies. Ship order: _shared.ts + config-schema.ts, then 0000_extensions.sql, then servers/groups/secrets, then tool_embedding/audit_event, then migrate.ts + bootstrap + the testcontainers check before anything else in the repo is written.
